title: Rigveda 9.35: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.35: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.35 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 680v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.35.1-6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 680v
translation.original_text:
1ā na̍ḥ pavasva̱ dhāra̍yā̱ pava̍māna ra̱yim pṛ̱thum | yayā̱ jyoti̍r vi̱dāsi̍ naḥ ||
2indo̍ samudramīṅkhaya̱ pava̍sva viśvamejaya | rā̱yo dha̱rtā na̱ oja̍sā ||
3tvayā̍ vī̱reṇa̍ vīravo̱ 'bhi ṣyā̍ma pṛtanya̱taḥ | kṣarā̍ ṇo a̱bhi vārya̍m ||
4pra vāja̱m indu̍r iṣyati̱ siṣā̍san vāja̱sā ṛṣi̍ḥ | vra̱tā vi̍dā̱na āyu̍dhā ||
5taṁ gī̱rbhir vā̍camīṅkha̱yam pu̍nā̱naṁ vā̍sayāmasi | soma̱ṁ jana̍sya̱ gopa̍tim ||
6viśvo̱ yasya̍ vra̱te jano̍ dā̱dhāra̱ dharma̍ṇa̱s pate̍ḥ | pu̱nā̱nasya̍ pra̱bhūva̍soḥ ||
translation.text:
1Pour forth on us abundant wealth, O Pavamâna, with thy stream. Wherewith thou mayest find us light
2O Indu, swayer of the sea, shaker of all things, flow thou on, Bearer of wealth to us with might.
3With thee for Hero, Valiant One! may we subdue our enemies: Let what is precious flow to us.
4Indu arouses strength the Sage who strives for victory, winning power, Discovering holy works and means.
5Mover of speech, we robe him with our songs as he is purified Soma, the Guardian of the folk;
6On whose way, Lord of Holy Law, most rich, as he is purified. The people all have set their hearts.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 680v (numbered 102v by the scribe) (OPenn image 681, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.34.3 ‹duhanti śakmanā payaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 681r (numbered 103r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.36.1 ‹vājī ni akramīt›. Verses 9.35.1-6 end on this page.

2indo iti | samudram-īṅkhaya | pavasva | viśvam-ejaya | rāyaḥ | dhartā | naḥ | ojasā
3tvayā | vīreṇa | vīra-vaḥ | abhi | syāma | pṛtanyataḥ | kṣara | naḥ | abhi | vāryam
4pra | vājam | induḥ | iṣyati | sisāsan | vāja-sāḥ | ṛṣiḥ | vratā | vidānaḥ | āyudhā
